security: For Memorystore for Redis Cluster, implement private VPC connectivity, AUTH/TLS where supported and secret rotation.

Audit Memorystore for Redis Cluster configuration and data access; protect its secrets, encryption keys and network paths according to workload classification.
operations: Monitor memory/CPU, ops/sec, latency, evictions, hot shards and replication health for Memorystore for Redis Cluster.
Version region, network, shard/replica count, node type, maintenance, auth/TLS and eviction, test representative load/failure and retain a rollback or recovery path.
Assign explicit Memorystore for Redis Cluster ownership for quotas, maintenance, regional failure, dependency health and incident response.
watchPoints: clients must support Redis Cluster redirection and multi-key operations are constrained by hash slots
Verify Memorystore for Redis Cluster regional availability, quotas, limits and compatibility before standardizing.

cost: provisioned shards/replicas, memory capacity and network.

Measure Memorystore for Redis Cluster cost per useful job, transaction, query or delivered workload rather than resource count alone.
alternatives: Memorystore for Redis Cluster — A managed Redis Cluster-compatible in-memory datastore with sharding, replicas and horizontal scale for high-throughput caching.
Memorystore for Valkey for open-source Valkey compatibility or standard cache tiers for smaller workloads — use when its stated design fit dominates.

services.summary: A managed in-memory Valkey service for low-latency caching and data structures using the open-source Redis-compatible ecosystem.
concepts: instance/cluster, node, keyspace and endpoint define the Memorystore for Valkey resource and data model.
The production path is application > Valkey protocol > in-memory keyspace > replica/failover > backing database on miss.
Memorystore for Valkey manages its service control plane; workload correctness, data classification and downstream behavior remain architecture responsibilities.
applicationFit: Choose Memorystore for Valkey when a managed in-memory Valkey service for low-latency caching and data structures using the open-source Redis-compatible ecosystem.
The strongest fit is a workload whose flow follows application > Valkey protocol > in-memory keyspace > replica/failover > backing database on miss.
Choose Memorystore for Redis Cluster where Redis Cluster compatibility is the established requirement instead when that alternative's operating model is the primary requirement.

services.summary: A horizontally scalable relational database with strong consistency, SQL, synchronous replication and multi-region configurations.
concepts: instance, instance configuration, database, table, key and processing unit define the Spanner resource and data model.
The production path is client transaction > Spanner API > split/key-range routing > replicated Paxos group > commit.
Spanner manages its service control plane; workload correctness, data classification and downstream behavior remain architecture responsibilities.
applicationFit: Choose Spanner when a horizontally scalable relational database with strong consistency, SQL, synchronous replication and multi-region configurations.
The strongest fit is a workload whose flow follows client transaction > Spanner API > split/key-range routing > replicated Paxos group > commit.
Choose Cloud SQL/AlloyDB when single-region PostgreSQL/MySQL compatibility matters more than horizontal global scale instead when that alternative's operating model is the primary requirement.
